sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

content.text:
Case N37: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 201x201x201 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case N37 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(201, 201, 201) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: peripheral nerve sheath tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 100/201 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: This appears to be a thigh/femur image with a bright lesion near vessels on the medial axial side, and in the coronal view at slice 100 there's a bright oval lesion centrally plus another bright subcutaneous blob toward the left edge lower down. I'm going to go through the slice sheets more carefully to confirm these findings.

content.text: sheet coronal 60–150/201 (12 slices) | v0 | tool calls 2/40, prompts 0/15
sheet axial 20–180/201 (12 slices) | v0 | tool calls 3/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm trying to pin down the exact location of the bright round mass at axial slice 93, medial to the femur, and distinguishing it from smaller bright structures near vessels and nerves on adjacent slices like coronal 93, axial 107, and axial 78.

content.text: axial 95/201 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 4/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm noting the roughly 20mm round mass, and that smaller bright structure nearby could be a vessel showing slow-flow hyperintensity rather than part of the lesion itself, so I'm weighing whether this is actually a peripheral nerve sheath tumor given its position relative to the femoral vessels rather than the sciatic nerve.

content.text: version v1 (parent v0) | volume 10.2 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 71–115, coronal 91–112, sagittal 110–134 | change +10.2 mL / 0.0 mL | tool calls 5/40, prompts 1/15 | point add (1 mark(s)) | image: axial 93, coronal 102, sagittal 122 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: The mask seems reasonable, spanning axial slices 71-115, about 45mm. I want to check the coronal view for where the mass starts, and look at axial 78 again since it showed a hazy bright region near the upper pole and a bright blob posteriorly that could be a vessel. Let me check the mask overlay on coronal slice 102 to clarify.

content.text: sagittal 122/201 | crop mask | marks fine | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 6/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
The mask on this sagittal looks fine, capturing the main mass with its fuzzy superior region near where the nerve seems to enter and a bright line marking the nerve exiting inferiorly. I also note axial slice 78 showed something hazy worth checking further.

Now let me pull up the coronal view with the mask overlaid to confirm the extent.

content.text: coronal 102/201 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 7/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: The mask looks good, and the tapering inferior tail including part of the exiting nerve is consistent with a tail sign, which fits the tumor. Now I'll check the candidates.

content.text:
v1 | 5 candidate(s): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong; judge each by the tissue inside its outline).
C1 add 10 mL, touches mask on its anterior, left and right sides, mostly posterior of the mask
C2 add 7.9 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly posterior of the mask
C3 add 6.0 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly posterior of the mask
C4 add 0.9 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
C5 add 0.8 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
candidate image: one row per candidate, columns axial / coronal / sagittal through the candidate (green outline = current mask, magenta outline + light tint = candidate; judge the tissue inside the magenta outline). Accept the ones that belong with seg_accept | tool calls 8/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I'm trying to identify structure C1 — it looks like an adjacent bright tubular shape posterior/lateral to the mass, elongated in the superior-inferior direction like a vessel, likely the femoral vein. On axial images I'm checking for a nearby flow void suggesting the femoral artery sits just below it.

Tracing the structure through consecutive slices (78, 93, 107, 122, 136, 165), it stays bright and round, continuing down toward the popliteal fossa where I'd expect the popliteal vein — slow-flow veins are commonly bright on fat-sat T2, which supports this being the femoral/popliteal vein rather than tumor or plexiform nerve sheath disease. I'm rejecting C1 as a mass component.

Now that the mask is essentially complete, I want to double-check the superior pole around axial slice 76 to make sure the less intense peripheral tissue is properly included in the segmentation.

content.text: axial 78/201 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 9/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Looking at axial slice 78, I notice a hazy brighter region extending medially beyond the mask's edge, roughly an oval spanning about 16mm, while the mask itself only captures the brighter core—this could represent partial volume averaging from the tumor's upper pole, or alternatively edema within the adjacent muscle.

Given the thick axial slices and the vertical streaking visible on coronal views, I suspect this superior pole is partially volumed rather than a distinct separate region, though comparing the tumor's exact location and width across different crops at slices 78 and 93 is tricky without a shared reference frame. I want to check the coronal view through the mass center at a different level to see whether the superior pole genuinely extends medially, and I'm considering examining axial slice 82 more closely with finer markup to resolve this.

content.text: axial 83/201 | crop mask | marks fine | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 10/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: Checking slice 83, the mask covers the mass well, and the hazy medial region at 78 is likely just partial volume effect from the upper pole. The segmentation looks good there, so now I want to verify the inferior extent around slice 110.

content.text: axial 108/201 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 11/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
At axial slice 108, the mask picks up a bright region corresponding to the nerve/tumor's lower pole, but it also includes a posterior extension into gray muscle tissue trailing toward the large bright vessel -- that looks like a leak since it's not actually bright signal. Given the sagittal view showed the tail tapering downward, I should erase that posterior extension as a false inclusion.

Since this leak likely spans several slices, maybe 104 to 112, I'm weighing whether to use seg_paint erase across that range or just place a negative point there, and I'd want fine marks to target it precisely.

content.text: axial 108/201 | crop mask | marks fine | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 12/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I'm trying to trace the mask outline more carefully, examining whether the posterior extension region between the bright nodule and the large vessel is actually gray muscle tissue rather than part of the highlighted area.

Since there's no negative point already inside the leak region, I'm considering drawing a negative scribble diagonally through it to erase the unwanted portion, though I'm wary it could also strip away parts of the nodule itself. The leak seems small, but given undo is available, trying the negative scribble across that diagonal seems worth the risk.

content.text: version v2 (parent v1) | volume 9.6 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 71–114, coronal 91–112, sagittal 111–134 | change +0.0 mL / -0.6 mL | tool calls 13/40, prompts 2/15 | scribble erase | image: axial 92, coronal 102, sagittal 122 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: The re-run model trimmed 0.6 mL total including small boundary adjustments throughout. Now I need to check axial slice 108.

content.text: axial 108/201 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 14/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
The leak is smaller now, just a thin residual tail, which seems acceptable. The bright region at axial 108 spanning that x-range with the hazy component is already covered by the mask, so that's fine too. I'm debating whether to use a small opening operation to clean up the thin tail, but that risks affecting real boundaries — it's possible this tail represents the actual nerve extending posteriorly, so I'll leave it alone.

It's tiny either way. Moving on to finish the review.

arguments.reason: Well-defined bright T2 mass medial thigh, mask follows boundary in all planes

content.text:
Final review of v2: volume 9.6 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 71–114, coronal 91–112, sagittal 111–134 | tool calls 15/40, prompts 2/15. The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. Candidates (second image): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong).
C1 add 6.9 mL, touches mask on its anterior, right and superior sides, mostly posterior of the mask
C2 add 3.8 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly superior of the mask
C3 add 2.0 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly posterior of the mask
C4 add 1.8 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly posterior of the mask
C5 add 1.6 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly superior of the mask
candidate image: one row per candidate, columns axial / coronal / sagittal through the candidate (green outline = current mask, magenta outline + light tint = candidate; judge the tissue inside the magenta outline). For each candidate decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept) or normal tissue (reject). Accept with seg_accept and call seg_finish again for a new review; if none belong, confirm with the review code. If everything is right, call seg_finish again with review_code "9941" to save it.

content.thinking:
I'm trying to sort out the orientation convention here - checking whether increasing axial index corresponds to superior or inferior, since the labeled slices suggest the knee region appears at higher indices, which seems to conflict with the "above mask" annotation at index 122.

I'm tracing the bright tubular structures in the coronal and sagittal views to figure out whether they represent the vessel versus the nerve entering/exiting the mass. The large superior tube around 8mm looks vessel-sized, likely the femoral vein, while the thinner inferior tail is probably the nerve - and I'm following the vessel's continuation through the popliteal region across the axial slices.

Checking C5 near the superior mask region too, but that also traces back to the vessel, so I can rule it out. I'm satisfied with the final read and ready to move to the review code.

arguments.reason: Well-defined bright T2 mass in medial thigh; mask follows its boundary in all planes; candidates were the adjacent vein and other vessels and were rejected

content.text: case N37 finished (confidence high); final mask saved from v2 | final volume 9.6 mL, components 1 (largest 100.0%) | tool calls 16/40, prompts 2/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

I've saved the mask of the peripheral nerve sheath tumor at 9.6 mL, in one piece, and I'm highly confident in it. The tumor is a sharply bounded, very bright oval mass in the inner thigh, next to the main vessels and about 2 cm across. It spans roughly 44 mm from top to bottom (axial slices 71–114), and its upper and lower tips taper along the nerve.

- **How it was built:** one positive point at the centre of the mass, viewed where it is largest (axial slice 95), captured the tumor.
- **One fix:** near the lower end (around axial slice 108) the mask had spread backward into darker muscle toward a large vein. A negative scribble removed 0.6 mL there. A tiny thin bit of that spread is still in the mask; I left it because it is very small.
- **Checks:** the outline followed the tumor edge in all three planes. The final review showed no tumor in the slices just past each end of the mask.
- **Rejected proposals:** I turned down all the automatic proposals for possibly missed tissue. The largest ran right alongside the mass, but it is a long tube about 8 mm wide that continues down to the vein behind the knee, so I judged it to be the femoral vein. The others were small vessels or other normal bright structures, not tumor.

I used 16 of 40 tool calls and 2 of 15 model prompts.
